groups.title: Doc staleness: decisions/0019-vendored-gif-codec-over-a-runtime-dependency — Consequences
groups.body:
**Doc:** decisions/0019-vendored-gif-codec-over-a-runtime-dependency | **Section:** Consequences | **Category:** staleness | **Misleads:** human engineer + coding agent | **Classification:** additive | **Confidence:** high

Verified-as-of: f93b63229ed1d580b82bcbb9d1e8ad0c71eb5f39

## Current State

`git cat-file -t 41dc8424f` and `git rev-list --all | grep ^41dc84` both come back empty: no object with this hash exists in the repo, shallow-clone artifacts aside. This is not a shallow-clone visibility gap — `git log --oneline --diff-filter=A -- plugin/bin/lib/gif/lzw.js plugin/bin/lib/gif/encoder.js plugin/bin/lib/gif/palette.js plugin/bin/lib/gif/png-decode.js` shows all four codec files were added in a single commit, `15553cf` ('[reconcile] archive run 2026-09-20T084158-record-2571'), already at their final/fixed content — there is no earlier commit touching these paths for a separate fix commit to modify. The cited hash was almost certainly a real in-worktree commit that this repo's own reconcile squashing process (documented elsewhere in this project) folded away when the pipeline run was archived, leaving a dangling reference. A reader — human or agent — who runs `git show 41dc8424f` to see the fix gets 'fatal: bad object 41dc8424f', not the promised diff.

## Deliverables

**Current:**
```
Fixed at `41dc8424f` and independently re-verified against real screenshots: 4 mid-stream resets exercised across both frames, decoding bit-exact at 921,600/921,600 pixels with 0 mismatches, while the pre-fix output fails the same decoder with a bitstream underrun.
```

**Proposed:**
```
Fixed within the same pipeline run; the standalone fix commit does not survive in this repo's history (folded away when the run was archived and squashed into `15553cf`, the commit that actually landed this codec — `41dc8424f` is not a resolvable object in this repository). Independently re-verified against real screenshots: 4 mid-stream resets exercised across both frames, decoding bit-exact at 921,600/921,600 pixels with 0 mismatches, while the pre-fix output fails the same decoder with a bitstream underrun.
```

## Acceptance Criteria

The commit hash cited as the LZW clear-code-width fix (`41dc8424f`) does not exist anywhere in this repository's history — replace the dangling reference with an accurate statement of where the fix actually landed.

## Release Note

No user-visible change — documentation accuracy fix.

_Filed by `/claude-tweaks:docs-health`. Close to resolve; label `wontfix` to suppress future reports of this finding._

groups.title: worktree-setup.md's catch-up log obligation has no home when no run directory exists
groups.body:
Surface: infra

## Current State

`_shared/worktree-setup.md`'s "Post-creation catch-up" section states: "When either merge actually advances the worktree's branch ... the calling procedure appends an entry to the run's `decisions.md` under its own heading." This assumes a pipeline run directory (and its `decisions.md`) already exists at the point the catch-up merge runs. But `specify/SKILL.md`'s own `needs:definition` redirect path explicitly states "brainstorming completes before any pipeline run directory exists" — and the ordinary interactive `/claude-tweaks:specify #N` entry point more generally has no `PIPELINE_RUN_DIR` at the point its own worktree is created and the catch-up procedure runs (a plain `/specify` invocation is not itself a `/flow`/`/dispatch`-orchestrated pipeline run). When this catch-up's merge genuinely advances the worktree branch (a real fast-forward pulling in upstream commits, not a no-op) under one of these no-run-dir call sites, the log obligation `worktree-setup.md` prescribes has nowhere to be written — the advance happens, but its audit trail is silently dropped.

## Deliverables

- Add an explicit no-run-dir branch to `_shared/worktree-setup.md`'s Post-creation catch-up "Log the correction when it changes anything" subsection: when no `$PIPELINE_RUN_DIR` resolves, either (a) write the advance to a standalone per-session log under `.claude-tweaks/` (a new, minimal mechanism), or (b) state explicitly that the calling skill must report the advance in its own Step 9/completion summary instead, and name which callers this applies to.
- Update `specify/SKILL.md` (or wherever it cites `worktree-setup.md`'s catch-up section for its own worktree-creation call site) to point at whichever branch is chosen, so the obligation has a stated home rather than being silently unsatisfiable for this call site.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `_shared/worktree-setup.md`'s Post-creation catch-up section states what happens to its own logging obligation when no pipeline run directory exists, rather than assuming one always does.
- A `/claude-tweaks:specify #N` invocation whose worktree-creation catch-up merge genuinely advances the branch reports that advance somewhere the user or a later auditor can find it (the skill's own summary, or a standalone log) — not silently.

## Release Note

Worktree setup now states where its catch-up correction is recorded when no pipeline run is active.

## Technical Approach

Decide between the two named branches in the Deliverables before implementing: a new minimal per-session standalone log (more mechanism, more durable) versus pushing the obligation onto each no-run-dir caller's own completion summary (less mechanism, relies on each caller remembering to report it). Given this repo's general preference for durable audit trails over caller-remembered reporting (per CLAUDE.md's auto-decision-log conventions elsewhere), lean toward option (a) unless the no-run-dir call sites are few enough that option (b) is reliably enforceable — enumerate every no-run-dir caller of `worktree-setup.md`'s catch-up section before choosing, since the choice should cover all of them, not just `/specify`.

### Key Files

- `plugin/skills/_shared/worktree-setup.md` — the Post-creation catch-up section's logging obligation
- `plugin/skills/specify/SKILL.md` — the citing call site to update once the branch is chosen

## Gotchas

- This is related to #2702 (also touches `worktree-setup.md`) — check for overlap before implementing either, since both modify the same file's Post-creation catch-up guidance.
- Enumerate every caller of `worktree-setup.md`'s catch-up section that might run with no `$PIPELINE_RUN_DIR` (not just `/specify`) before deciding the fix's scope — a fix that only covers `/specify`'s call site could leave the same silent-drop gap open elsewhere.

## Original request

groups.title: Add a pre-launch checklist lens for AI/vibe-coded sites
groups.body:
Surface: infra

**Related:** #2624, #2692

## Current State

No standing pre-launch checklist exists across `/review`, `/code-health`, or `/build` for AI-generated sites. A documented 20-item pre-publish checklist covers custom 404, meta title/description per page, OG image, favicon, robots.txt, sitemap.xml, alt text, mobile breakpoints, form/loading states, thank-you page, privacy policy, terms, cookie banner, analytics, real contact info, and compressed images.

## Deliverables

- Turn the 20-item list into a policy-row set for `/code-health` or a final `/review` pass before a site ships.
- Group items by cheap-to-automate (sitemap.xml, robots.txt, alt text, image compression) vs. needs-human-judgment (privacy policy, terms).

## Acceptance Criteria

- Running the lens against a sample site reports pass/fail for all 20 items.

## Release Note

Added a pre-launch code-health check for AI-built sites covering commonly missed launch items such as sitemaps, meta tags, and legal pages.

## Technical Approach

Follow the precedent #2624 set for the sibling pre-launch security checklist: a `/claude-tweaks:code-health` focus vertical (`focus=prelaunch`) made of a candidate generator, a criterion entry, a criterion fragment, and the focus-mode registration rows. The generator emits candidates only for the mechanically detectable items (sitemap.xml, robots.txt, favicon, custom 404, per-page meta title/description, OG image, `alt` attributes, image sizes over a compression threshold); the fragment lists every one of the 20 items and marks the rest (privacy policy, terms, cookie banner, analytics, real contact info, mobile breakpoints, form/loading states, thank-you page) as needs-manual-check, so the report separates "verified" from "a human should confirm".

### Key Files

- `plugin/bin/lib/code-health/candidates-prelaunch.js` — new focus generator: file/markup-presence candidates for the automatable items, with a Coverage block header like `candidates-security-hardening.js`
- `plugin/bin/lib/code-health/focus-generators.js` — register the `prelaunch` focus
- `plugin/bin/lib/code-health/criteria.js` — `prelaunch` criterion entry pointing at its fragment
- `plugin/skills/_shared/criteria-prelaunch.md` — new criterion fragment: all 20 items, split into automatable vs. needs-manual-check, with severity calibration
- `plugin/skills/code-health/focus-mode.md` — Criterion-pinning table row and Coverage-section pointer for `prelaunch` (both required whenever `FOCUS_GENERATORS` gains a key)
- `tests/bin-lib/code-health/candidates-prelaunch.test.js` — generator tests, mirroring `candidates-security-hardening.test.js`

## Gotchas

- Keep the automatable/manual split explicit in the output — a report that conflates "verified automatically" with "a human should confirm" overstates what the check did.
- Items needing a live render (mobile breakpoints, form/loading states) are needs-manual-check in the fragment, not generator candidates — the acceptance criterion's pass/fail for all 20 items allows a "needs manual check" outcome.
- The generator's Coverage block must state its reach honestly (IL-110): presence of a file or tag, not its quality.
- focus-mode.md makes a registry key without a Criterion-pinning row a fail-loud stop — land both in the same change.

## Original request

Add a pre-launch checklist lens for AI/vibe-coded sites

Current State:
- No standing pre-launch checklist exists across /review, /code-health, or /build for AI-generated sites.
- A reel lists 20 concrete pre-publish checks: custom 404, meta title/description per page, OG image, favicon, robots.txt, sitemap.xml, alt text, mobile breakpoints, form/loading states, thank-you page, privacy policy, terms, cookie banner, analytics, real contact info, compressed images.

Deliverables:
- Turn the 20-item list into a policy-row set for /code-health or a final /review pass before a site ships.
- Group items by cheap-to-automate (sitemap.xml, robots.txt, alt text, image compression) vs. needs-human-judgment (privacy policy, terms).

Acceptance Criteria:
- Running the lens against a sample site reports pass/fail for all 20 items.

Source: https://www.instagram.com/reel/DcEqXsySUaP/

groups.title: Add a lightweight perf-audit lens (images, unused loads, measure-first)
groups.body:
Surface: infra

**Related:** #2693

## Current State

claude-tweaks has no standing performance-audit lens — `/code-health` and `/review` don't check image format, unused resource loading, or a measured baseline. A 3-minute speed-audit checklist (image format conversion, unused-resource flagging, PageSpeed Insights baseline before changing anything) exists as an established, low-cost pattern worth codifying as a lens.

## Deliverables

- Add a perf-audit lens/policy row (image-format check, unused-resource flag, PageSpeed Insights baseline) to `/code-health` or `/review`.
- Keep it a fast, free check — no new paid tooling.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Running the lens against a sample app reports pass/fail for at least the three checks above (image format, unused resources, PageSpeed Insights baseline).

## Release Note

Code and visual reviews now flag oversized or legacy-format images and unused loaded resources, and recommend measuring page speed before optimizing.

## Technical Approach

Two homes, split by what each can observe. The static checks — a legacy-format or oversized image added to the diff, and a script/stylesheet/font loaded but unused — join `/claude-tweaks:review`'s lens 3d (Performance) in `plugin/skills/review/step3-lens-dispatch.md` as question bullets. The measure-first rule — record a baseline with a free tool (Lighthouse CLI, or the PageSpeed Insights API's free tier) before changing anything for performance — joins `/claude-tweaks:visual-review`'s `page-mode.md` Step 4 Performance subsection, which already owns runtime vitals. No new paid dependency.

### Key Files

- `plugin/skills/review/step3-lens-dispatch.md` — lens 3d (Performance) gains the image-format/oversized-asset and unused-loaded-resource bullets
- `plugin/skills/visual-review/page-mode.md` — Step 4's Performance subsection gains the measure-first baseline (free Lighthouse CLI or PageSpeed Insights) before any performance fix

## Gotchas

- "No new paid tooling" is an explicit constraint — Lighthouse CLI and the PageSpeed Insights API free tier both stay within it; name the tool in the text.
- This is a lightweight addition, not a full performance-audit subsystem — scope the three named checks only.
- page-mode's Performance subsection says vitals are unavailable from its own browser session; the measure-first rule is guidance to run a baseline, not a claim that the walk measures it.

## Original request

Add a lightweight perf-audit lens (images, unused loads, measure-first)

Current State:
- claude-tweaks has no standing performance-audit lens; /code-health and /review don't check image format, unused resource loading, or a measured baseline.
- A reel gives a 3-minute speed-audit checklist: convert non-PNG-appropriate images, cut unused loaded resources, and run PageSpeed Insights before changing anything.

Deliverables:
- Add a perf-audit lens/policy row (image-format check, unused-resource flag, PageSpeed Insights baseline) to /code-health or /review.
- Keep it a fast, free check — no new paid tooling.

Acceptance Criteria:
- Running the lens against a sample app reports pass/fail for at least the three checks above.

Source: https://www.instagram.com/reel/DcFfEBOxlKZ/

groups.title: Flag polling-vs-realtime and duplicate-version anti-patterns
groups.body:
Surface: infra

## Current State
Two recurring coding-agent anti-patterns have been identified from an external source (a transcribed Instagram Reel from a developer who has shipped 15+ AI-built apps):

1. **Polling instead of realtime push** — agents building a data flow that needs live updates default to fixed-interval polling (e.g. `setInterval` fetches every few seconds) instead of a realtime push/subscription mechanism when the backend already supports one (e.g. a Supabase/Convex subscription, a websocket, SSE). This looks fine in testing but drains battery and degrades frame rate under real usage.
2. **Duplicate "v2" files instead of in-place edits** — agents avoid replacing working code in place, instead layering a `v2`/duplicate-suffixed file or function on top "just in case." This leaves dead code around, and the agent loses track of which version is actually live, leading to circular, self-breaking edits on later requests.

Anti-pattern 2 is already a standing instruction in this repo's own CLAUDE.md ("don't use feature flags or backwards-compatibility shims when you can just change the code" — see the Philosophy/Don'ts sections) — the external source is independent confirmation that the same failure mode is common enough across coding agents generally to be worth a dedicated automated review check, not just a written instruction the agent might drift from under pressure.

Neither anti-pattern currently has an automated review-lens check.

## Deliverables
1. Add a review-lens check that flags a newly introduced fixed-interval polling loop (`setInterval`/`setTimeout` recursion, or an equivalent polling construct) against a data source that already exposes or could reasonably expose a realtime push/subscription mechanism.
2. Add a review-lens check that flags a newly created file or function with a version-suffix name pattern (`v2`, `-new`, `-copy`, `_updated`, etc.) sitting alongside an unremoved original that the diff did not delete or fully migrate away from.
3. Document that these two checks formalize the existing CLAUDE.md "change code in place" instruction into an automated check, rather than relying on the instruction alone.

## Acceptance Criteria
- The polling check flags a sample diff that adds a fixed-interval polling loop against a realtime-capable backend.
- The polling check does not flag polling against a data source with no realtime alternative available (e.g. a third-party REST API with no push option).
- The duplicate-version check flags a sample diff that introduces a `v2`-suffixed (or equivalent) file/function alongside its unremoved original.
- The duplicate-version check does not flag a legitimate versioned artifact (e.g. an API route intentionally versioned as `/v2/` for external consumers) — the check targets abandoned/duplicated internal code, not a deliberate external contract.
- Documentation for the review-lens (or the relevant skill's checklist) states that these two checks formalize the existing CLAUDE.md instruction into an automated check.

## Release Note

Code review now flags new polling loops where realtime updates are available, and leftover "v2"-style duplicate copies of code.

## Technical Approach

Both checks land in `/claude-tweaks:review`'s lens definitions (`plugin/skills/review/step3-lens-dispatch.md`, "Lens definitions (3a-3f)"), as new question bullets matching those lenses' existing style. The polling check joins 3d (Performance): flag a newly introduced fixed-interval polling loop (`setInterval`/recursive `setTimeout`, or equivalent) against a source that exposes a push/subscription mechanism. The duplicate-version check joins 3a (Convention Compliance): flag a new version-suffixed file or function (`v2`, `-new`, `-copy`, `_updated`) beside an original the diff neither deleted nor migrated away from. Each bullet states its false-positive guard inline (no realtime alternative; a deliberately versioned external contract).

### Key Files

- `plugin/skills/review/step3-lens-dispatch.md` — lens 3d (Performance) gains the polling check; lens 3a (Convention Compliance) gains the duplicate-version check; each carries its false-positive guard

## Gotchas

- The duplicate-version check must not fire on legitimate, deliberately-versioned external-facing artifacts (API routes, published package majors) — only on abandoned/duplicated internal code from indecisive in-place-edit avoidance.
- The polling check must not fire when no realtime alternative exists for the given backend/data source — polling is the correct choice there, not an anti-pattern.
- `step3-lens-dispatch.md` feeds a composed dispatch-contract bundle (#2019); run `npm test` for the prose/byte pins that cover it.

## Original request

Flag polling-vs-realtime and duplicate-version anti-patterns

Current State:
- Reel (hook-only caption; transcribed), from a developer who has shipped 15+ AI-built apps, names two recurring coding-agent anti-patterns: (1) agents default to polling the server every few seconds instead of using a realtime push mechanism (e.g. Supabase/Convex subscriptions), draining battery and degrading frame rate under real usage even though it feels fine in testing; (2) agents avoid replacing code in place, instead layering a "v2" on top of the working version "just in case," which leaves dead code around and causes the agent to lose track of which version is live, leading to circular, self-breaking edits on later requests.
- The second anti-pattern is already addressed as a standing instruction in this session's own CLAUDE.md guidance ("don't use feature flags or backwards-compatibility shims when you can just change the code") — this reel is independent confirmation the same failure mode is common enough to be worth a dedicated automated check, not just a written instruction the agent might drift from.

Deliverables:
- Add a review-lens check for: (a) new realtime data flows implemented as fixed-interval polling instead of push/subscription where the backend supports it; (b) newly created "v2"/duplicate-suffixed files or functions sitting alongside an unremoved original.

Acceptance Criteria:
- Check flags a sample polling loop and a sample duplicate-version file pair.
- Docs note this formalizes an existing CLAUDE.md instruction into an automated check rather than relying on the instruction alone.

Source: https://www.instagram.com/reel/DcW5UU5SUaB/

groups.title: Evaluate adopting an Intent.MD-style pre-build intent file
groups.body:
Surface: infra

## Current State

Anthropic has described a file convention, intent.MD, that precedes and guides a feature's development lifecycle — a single file with sections like Author, Status, and Problem that an agent reads before starting a build. claude-tweaks currently starts build work from an issue/spec record (via `/specify`) with no equivalent lightweight, structured intent-capture step ahead of that.

## Deliverables

- Assess whether an intent.MD-style file would improve the current spec/build flow (e.g. as a precursor to `/claude-tweaks:specify`), and if so, propose its field structure and where it's read from.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A written adopt/discard decision, with reasoning either way.

## Release Note

Recorded a decision on whether to adopt an Intent.MD-style pre-build intent file (no user-visible change).

## Technical Approach

This is an evaluation record, not a build record — the deliverable IS the written decision, recorded as an ADR under `docs/decisions/` (a rejected option is a valid ADR outcome). Compare intent.MD's stated purpose (Author/Status/Problem fields read before a build starts) against what `/claude-tweaks:capture` and `/claude-tweaks:specify`'s shaping-mode body sections (`## Current State`, `## Deliverables`, `## Acceptance Criteria`) already capture, to judge whether intent.MD adds net-new value or duplicates a step this repo already has. Read the source article's description of intent.MD's actual field set and workflow position before judging overlap. The compared skill files are read, not edited, so they are not Key Files.

### Key Files

- `docs/decisions/0020-intent-file-evaluation.md` — new: the written adopt/discard decision (take the next free number under `docs/decisions/` at build time)

## Gotchas

- The Acceptance Criteria only require a written decision, not an implementation either way — if the decision is "adopt," a follow-up record should be filed for the actual implementation rather than folding both into this one.
- Judge genuinely, not performatively — this repo's existing `/capture` → `/specify` flow may already cover intent.MD's value; a reflexive "adopt everything Anthropic describes" isn't the goal here.

## Original request

Evaluate adopting an Intent.MD-style pre-build intent file

Current State:
- Anthropic has described a file convention, intent.MD, that precedes and guides a feature's development lifecycle -- a single file with sections like Author, Status, and Problem that an agent reads before starting a build.
- claude-tweaks currently starts build work from an issue/spec record (via /specify) with no equivalent lightweight, structured intent-capture step ahead of that.

Deliverables:
- Assess whether an intent.MD-style file would improve the current spec/build flow (e.g. as a precursor to /claude-tweaks:specify), and if so, propose its field structure and where it's read from.

Acceptance Criteria:
- A written adopt/discard decision, with reasoning either way.

Source: https://medium.com/@joe.njenga/claude-code-intent-md-new-anthropic-blueprint-for-building-great-software-e2f0c8a5eac2

groups.title: Audit CLAUDE.md files against Anthropic's own <200-line context-engineering guidance
groups.body:
Surface: infra

## Current State

Anthropic's own context-engineering guidance says Claude Code's own system prompt was cut by over 80% for Opus 5/Fable 5 with no measurable eval loss, and targets CLAUDE.md files at roughly under 200 lines. An independent audit of a real 388-skill repository found its CLAUDE.md at 829 lines / 110KB — 4x over that target, with one section alone consuming 86,630 characters. A separate piece from the same author on writing a good global CLAUDE.md argues each rule should name a specific past failure rather than state vague preferences (e.g. "write clean code"). claude-tweaks generates and maintains CLAUDE.md content across projects with no check against this size or authoring guidance. Notably, this repo's own CLAUDE.md already practices a related discipline manually — its `## Don'ts` section states "Full rule list now lives in docs/donts.md (moved out of this always-loaded file to fit the 150-line budget)" — so a lint/audit check would formalize and enforce a budget this repo already tries to hold ad hoc.

Update (shaping, 2026-09-30): the line-count half already exists. harness-health's check 4 (`plugin/skills/harness-health/judge-procedure.md`, "Tiered line-budget check") puts CLAUDE.md in the always-loaded tier and compares it against `harness-health-always-loaded-budget`, default 150 (`_shared/policy-schema.md`). Missing: a single-runaway-section signal, and the specific-failure authoring principle in `init`'s CLAUDE.md template. The record is rescoped to that delta.

## Deliverables

1. Add a runaway-section signal to harness-health's tiered line-budget check (check 4) in `plugin/skills/harness-health/judge-procedure.md` and `plugin/skills/_shared/harness-health-analysis.md`: flag a CLAUDE.md whose largest `##` section exceeds a stated share of the file's lines, even when the file is under budget.
2. Add the "each rule names a specific past failure, not a vague preference" principle, citing Anthropic's context-engineering guidance, to `plugin/skills/init/claude-md-template.md`'s authoring guidance.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Check 4 in both `judge-procedure.md` and `_shared/harness-health-analysis.md` describes the runaway-section signal, its threshold, and how the section share is computed (heading-bounded line counts).
2. The signal reports as a `template-conformance` finding framed as a flag for review, never a hard failure.
3. The `harness-health-always-loaded-budget` default (150) is unchanged.
4. `plugin/skills/init/claude-md-template.md` states the specific-past-failure principle and cites its source.
5. `npm test` passes.

## Release Note

Harness health now flags a CLAUDE.md dominated by one runaway section, and generated CLAUDE.md guidance asks each rule to name a specific past failure.

## Technical Approach

harness-health check 4 already classifies CLAUDE.md into the always-loaded tier and compares `wc -l` against `harness-health-always-loaded-budget` (default 150, stricter than the 200-line guidance). Extend that check with a second mechanical signal: scan `##` heading boundaries and flag when the largest section exceeds a stated share of the file (e.g. 40% of its lines), even when the total is under budget — reported as the same `template-conformance` finding, a flag for review, never a gate. Mirror the change in `_shared/harness-health-analysis.md`'s check 4 so the two stay identical. Separately, add the specific-failure principle to `plugin/skills/init/claude-md-template.md`, the origin template dimensions 7 and 8 already read for `claude-md` targets.

### Key Files

- `plugin/skills/harness-health/judge-procedure.md` — check 4 (tiered line-budget) gains the runaway-section signal

groups.title: Add GDPR account-deletion vs. backup-retention check
groups.body:
Surface: infra

## Current State
Deleting a user from the production database on account deletion leaves their personal data intact in rolling database backups (e.g. a 30-day retention window), which can violate GDPR right-to-erasure. Rewriting, decrypting, and recompressing terabytes of backup data to scrub one user on every deletion request is operationally expensive and can overwhelm production systems. Cryptographic erasure — encrypting each user's sensitive data with a unique per-user key and destroying only that key on deletion — makes the backup copy unreadable without ever touching the backup itself. This project's pre-launch security hardening checklist (#2624, open, priority:medium) is being built for AI-built apps but currently has no check for this specific data-retention/right-to-erasure gap.

Update (shaping, 2026-09-30): #2624 has shipped as `plugin/skills/_shared/criteria-security-hardening.md`, and its "Scope boundary" section explicitly excludes this check. It therefore lands standalone, in the `privacy-pii` criterion.

## Deliverables
1. Add a data-retention/right-to-erasure check — as a new row in the pre-launch security checklist being built under #2624, or as its own standalone policy row if #2624 lands first without this scope — that flags whether the app's backup/retention strategy leaves deleted users' data readable, and whether per-user field-level encryption is in place for data that lands in backups.
2. Document the cryptographic-erasure pattern (per-user key encryption + key destruction on deletion) as the recommended fix when a project keeps rolling backups containing user PII.
3. Ship a copy-paste prompt, matching this pipeline's existing pattern for this class of check, that walks a codebase through checking for this specific gap.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Running the check against a sample app flags whether a deleted user's data would remain readable in existing backups after an account-deletion flow runs.
2. The shipped documentation/policy content notes its relationship to the pre-launch security checklist (#2624) so the two records' scope doesn't duplicate — whichever lands first, the other references it rather than re-deriving the same check.
3. The check (and its copy-paste prompt) works standalone and as a step within `/claude-tweaks:review` or a security-review pass.
4. The documented recommended-fix pattern (cryptographic erasure) is described generically enough to apply across storage backends, not tied to one specific database or cloud vendor's backup product.

## Release Note

Added a privacy check that flags when deleted users' data stays readable in backups, with a cryptographic-erasure fix pattern.

## Technical Approach

#2624 has shipped (`plugin/skills/_shared/criteria-security-hardening.md`) and its Scope boundary explicitly excludes this check, so it lands standalone in `plugin/skills/_shared/criteria-privacy-pii.md` — the generalist `privacy-pii` criterion (`criteria.js`) that already applies to frontend/backend/data areas. Add a "What to flag" bullet for the concrete code pattern (an account-deletion path that removes live rows while backups keep plaintext PII, with no per-user key to destroy), a severity-calibration entry, and a copy-paste prompt in the style of criteria-security-hardening.md's "Copy-paste prompts" section. Document cryptographic erasure (per-user key encryption, key destruction on deletion) generically as the recommended fix. Repoint criteria-security-hardening.md's Scope boundary bullet at the new home.

### Key Files

- `plugin/skills/_shared/criteria-privacy-pii.md` — new backup-retention-vs-erasure flag, severity calibration entry, and copy-paste prompt
- `plugin/skills/_shared/criteria-security-hardening.md` — its Scope boundary bullet for this check repointed at `criteria-privacy-pii.md`

## Gotchas

- `criteria-privacy-pii.md` already says to flag only the concrete code pattern, not the regulatory question — phrase the new flag as a code/config pattern (a deletion path plus a plaintext backup), never as a GDPR compliance verdict.
- Keep the fix pattern vendor-neutral (acceptance criterion 4).

## Original request

Add GDPR account-deletion vs. backup-retention check

Current State:
- Deleting a user from the production database on account deletion leaves their personal data intact in rolling database backups (e.g. a 30-day retention window), which can violate GDPR right-to-erasure.
- Rewriting, decrypting, and recompressing terabytes of backup data to scrub one user on every deletion request is operationally expensive and can overwhelm production systems.
- Cryptographic erasure — encrypting each user's sensitive data with a unique per-user key and destroying only that key on deletion — makes the backup copy unreadable without ever touching the backup itself.

Deliverables:
- Add a data-retention/right-to-erasure check to the existing pre-launch security checklist (issue #2624) or as its own policy row: does the app's backup/retention strategy leave deleted users' data readable, and is per-user field-level encryption in place for data that lands in backups?
- Document the cryptographic-erasure pattern as the recommended fix when a project keeps rolling backups containing user PII.
- Ship a copy-paste prompt, matching the pipeline's existing pattern, that walks a codebase through checking for this gap.

Acceptance Criteria:
- Running the check against a sample app flags whether a deleted user's data would remain readable in existing backups.
- Docs note the relationship to the pre-launch security checklist (#2624) so scope doesn't duplicate.
- Works standalone and as a step within /review or /security-review.

groups.title: Add classic friction-reduction UX laws to the review lens
groups.body:
Surface: infra

**Related:** #2655, #2706, #2707

## Current State

The design-review lens has no checks tied to the classic conversion/friction heuristics: choice count (Hick's Law), tap-target/CTA affordance (Fitts's Law), navigation familiarity (Jacob's Law), or chunked identifiers like phone numbers and codes (Miller's Law). No check for a journey's peak/end moments (Peak-End Rule), spatial grouping of related controls (Proximity), or a single visually distinct emphasis element (Von Restorff Effect).

Update (shaping, 2026-09-30): #2655 already shipped `plugin/skills/visual-review/ux-heuristics-lens.md`, whose rows cover all seven heuristics this record names (Reduce choices per screen, Use large targets, Favor familiar patterns, Chunk content, End flows memorably, Group related info, Highlight the primary action). What is missing is the record's second deliverable: naming each law, so violations are self-documenting. The record is rescoped to that delta.

## Deliverables

1. Add the law's name to each of the seven existing `ux-heuristics-lens.md` rows that already cover it: Reduce choices per screen → Hick's law; Use large targets → Fitts's law; Favor familiar patterns → Jakob's law; Chunk content → Miller's law; End flows memorably → peak-end rule; Group related info → law of common region / proximity; Highlight the primary action → Von Restorff effect.
2. Extend the Chunk content row's example to cover unchunked numeric identifiers (e.g. a 16-digit code rendered as one unbroken run).
3. Add one sentence to the lens's "Reporting a finding" section: a finding cites its row's law by name when the row has one, so violations are self-documenting.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Each of the seven rows listed in Deliverable 1 names its law.
2. The Chunk content row's example covers an unchunked numeric identifier.
3. The checklist still has 20 rows — no duplicate row is added for a law an existing row already covers.
4. "Reporting a finding" asks a finding to cite the row's law by name.
5. `npm test` passes.

## Release Note

UX heuristics findings now name the classic UX law behind each check, such as Hick's law or Fitts's law.

## Technical Approach

A text edit to `plugin/skills/visual-review/ux-heuristics-lens.md`: append the law's name to the Heuristic cell (or the start of "What it flags") of the seven rows #2655 already shipped, extend the Chunk content example to cover numeric identifiers, and add one sentence to "Reporting a finding" asking a finding to cite the law when its row names one. No new rows and no new mechanism.

### Key Files

- `plugin/skills/visual-review/ux-heuristics-lens.md` — law names added to seven existing rows; Chunk content example extended; Reporting section updated

## Gotchas

- #2706 and #2707 edit the same file; consider landing them together.
- Some laws (peak-end rule, Von Restorff effect) are more subjective than others (Fitts's law, Miller's law); the citation names the law without implying more mechanical certainty than the row's manual-inspection framing allows.
- The source reel spells it "Jacob's law"; the correct name is Jakob's law (after Jakob Nielsen).

## Original request

Add classic friction-reduction UX laws to the review lens

Current State:
- The design-review lens has no checks tied to the classic conversion/friction heuristics: choice count (Hick's Law), tap-target/CTA affordance (Fitts's Law), navigation familiarity (Jacob's Law), or chunked identifiers like phone numbers and codes (Miller's Law).
- No check for a journey's peak/end moments (Peak-End Rule), spatial grouping of related controls (Proximity), or a single visually distinct emphasis element (Von Restorff Effect).

Deliverables:
- A policy row per law: too-many-options, small/ambiguous primary actions, unfamiliar nav patterns, unchunked numeric IDs, no memorable peak/end step, ungrouped related controls, no standout CTA.
- Cite the law by name in the check's explanation so violations are self-documenting.

Acceptance Criteria:
- Running the lens on a form with 10+ ungrouped choices or an unchunked ID field flags the specific law violated.

Source: https://www.instagram.com/p/DddqpGrS-lI/

groups.title: simplify dispatch: caller can observe a still-in-flight async Task write as "done"
groups.body:
Surface: infra
Origin: reflect light from #2621
Defer-reason: tangential

**Related:** #2533, #2714

## Current State

`/claude-tweaks:simplify`'s Step 2 dispatches the `code-simplifier:code-simplifier` subagent via the `Agent` tool, which runs asynchronously: the dispatch returns immediately, and the agent's final state is only known once its completion notification (its reply ending in the `STATUS:` line Step 2's own output template requires) arrives. The paragraph at `plugin/skills/simplify/SKILL.md:87` ("When dispatched with file-path scope …") tells the caller to "diff them against its own change scope and revert anything outside it" but never says *when* — nothing ties the check to that completion signal.

During record #2621's review Step 5, the caller ran `git status` shortly after dispatch, saw one out-of-scope file modified, reverted it (`git checkout --`), and moved on. The agent was still running: it went on to write a second, larger wave of out-of-scope edits (a `cmdNextTarget` refactor in `harness-health.js`) that a later, unrelated check caught and a second `git checkout --` pass had to clean up. A diff-and-revert check run before the agent has returned has no guarantee it is looking at final state.

## Deliverables

1. Amend the file-path-scope paragraph in `plugin/skills/simplify/SKILL.md` Step 2 so the diff-and-revert check has an explicit precondition: it runs only after the subagent's reply — carrying Step 2's required `STATUS:` line — has been received, never against an ad hoc `git status` poll taken while the dispatch may still be running.
2. State the consequence of a premature check in the same paragraph, briefly: edits the agent writes after an early revert survive into the caller's commit.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `plugin/skills/simplify/SKILL.md` Step 2's file-path-scope paragraph names receipt of the subagent's final reply (its `STATUS:` line) as the precondition for the diff-and-revert check.
2. The same paragraph says a working-tree check taken before that reply is not the agent's final state and must not drive a revert.
3. No other step of `/claude-tweaks:simplify` changes, and `npm test` passes (prose conformance suites pin skill text repo-wide).

## Release Note

Clarified that /simplify's out-of-scope revert check waits for the simplifier agent to finish, so late edits can no longer slip past it.

## Technical Approach

A prose-only change to one paragraph. The record's original second option — a new "wait for this dispatch" primitive — is not taken: the completion notification already exists and is the plugin's established "agent is done" signal (`plugin/skills/dispatch/task-prompt.md` forbids ending a turn to wait on one, which is compatible — the caller simply does the check in the turn that receives the reply). Naming the existing signal as the precondition closes the race without new machinery.

### Key Files

- `plugin/skills/simplify/SKILL.md` — Step 2's file-path-scope paragraph gains the completion-precondition sentence

## Gotchas

- Do not add polling or sleep-loop guidance — the fix is ordering (check after the reply), not waiting harder.
- `/claude-tweaks:review` Step 5 dispatches `/simplify` and is where the race surfaced; its own text defers to Step 2 here, so no edit is needed there — confirm with a grep for the Step 2 paragraph's wording before assuming otherwise.

## Original request

simplify dispatch: caller can observe a still-in-flight async Task write as "done"

Origin: reflect light from #2621
Defer-reason: tangential

## Current State

`/claude-tweaks:simplify`'s Step 2 dispatches the `code-simplifier:code-simplifier` subagent via the `Agent` tool, which is asynchronous — the dispatch call returns immediately with an `agentId`, and the caller is told "you know nothing about its results until [a] notification arrives." Step 2's own guidance ("Before committing the returned changes, the caller should diff them against its own change scope and revert anything outside it") assumes the caller can check `git status`/`git diff` once, right after dispatch, and see the agent's *final* state. During this review's Step 5 (record #2621), the caller (this flow run) checked `git status` shortly after dispatch, saw one out-of-scope file modified, reverted it (`git checkout --`), and moved on — only to find on a later, unrelated check that the agent had *continued writing* after that revert, producing a second, larger wave of out-of-scope edits (a `cmdNextTarget` refactor in `harness-health.js`) that required a second `git checkout --` pass to reach a clean tree. Because the Agent tool's async notification is the only reliable "the agent is truly done" signal, and the coordinating call cannot poll/sleep-loop for it, a caller that does the diff-and-revert check on its own initiative (rather than waiting for the completion notification) has no guarantee it is looking at final state.

## Deliverables

Clarify `skills/simplify/SKILL.md` Step 2's diff-and-revert guidance to state explicitly that the revert check must run only after the dispatch's completion notification has been received (not on an ad hoc `git status` poll), or provide an explicit "wait for this dispatch" primitive callers can use without violating the "never end this turn waiting" constraint documented elsewhere in this same plugin's dispatch guidance.

## Acceptance Criteria

`skills/simplify/SKILL.md`'s Step 2 names the completion-notification requirement (or an equivalent wait primitive) as a precondition for the diff-and-revert check, so a caller following the instructions as written cannot repeat this race.

groups.title: Add a notification-badge design checklist to the UI review lens
groups.body:
Surface: infra

**Related:** #2707, #2709

## Current State

The Impeccable/design-review lens has no explicit rules for count badges vs. status dots (when to combine, when they collide). No guidance distinguishes "something changed" (dot) from "how much" (number), or governs badge color semantics (red = act now, green = online). No rule flags a badge that lingers after the user has already viewed the item, or a count that resets to zero instead of ticking down.

## Deliverables

- A policy row (or lens check) for badge/dot usage: one signal per element, color tied to meaning, clears on view.
- A check for "badge everything" anti-patterns that dilute color meaning.
- Reference the source technique inline so the check has a rationale, not just a rule.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Running the design-review lens on a UI with a badge flags a dual dot+counter on the same element.
- The check explains why (noise / trained-to-ignore) rather than just failing silently.

## Release Note

The UX heuristics lens now flags confusing notification badges: doubled dot-and-count signals, colors without meaning, and badges that never clear.

Add the badge/dot rules as rows in `/claude-tweaks:visual-review`'s UX heuristics lens (`plugin/skills/visual-review/ux-heuristics-lens.md`, the plugin-owned UI checklist that page mode Step 4 applies and `/claude-tweaks:review` uses for UI-affecting diffs), in its existing Heuristic | What it flags | Example violation shape. `design-wrapper/modes/` is not the home: it routes to Impeccable and to project-local critics and owns no checklist of its own. Rows: one signal per element (flag a status dot and a count badge on the same element), color tied to meaning (flag badge colors that do not map to a stated convention, and "badge everything" dilution), and clears on view (flag a badge that lingers after the item was viewed, or a count that resets instead of ticking down). Each row's "What it flags" carries the one-line rationale (noise; users trained to ignore), per the Acceptance Criteria.

groups.title: Add a typographic-system checklist to the UI review lens
groups.body:
Surface: infra

**Related:** #2706, #2709

## Current State

The design-review lens has no check for typographic-system discipline: font count, a fixed type-scale ratio, or a capped weight count. No rule catches hand-picked pixel sizes, uniform line-height across headings/body, or unbounded paragraph measure (characters per line). No check for tabular figures on numeric/price/timer UI, which is what stops columns from wobbling on data updates. Competitive note: a third-party Claude Code plugin ("UX engine") designs the screen before coding and audits diffs for an "AI look" — worth knowing about as adjacent to Impeccable.

## Deliverables

- A policy row for a bounded type scale (one ratio, capped sizes/weights) and capped line length (45-75 characters).
- A check for tabular-nums usage on numeric UI.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Running the lens on a UI with unbounded font sizes or an unmeasured paragraph flags it with the specific rule violated.

## Release Note

The UX heuristics lens now checks typography: a bounded type scale, readable line length, and tabular figures on numeric UI.

## Technical Approach

Add the checks as rows in `/claude-tweaks:visual-review`'s UX heuristics lens (`plugin/skills/visual-review/ux-heuristics-lens.md`, the plugin-owned UI checklist page mode Step 4 applies and `/claude-tweaks:review` uses for UI-affecting diffs), in its existing Heuristic | What it flags | Example violation shape. `design-wrapper/modes/` is not the home: it routes to Impeccable and project-local critics and owns no checklist. Rows: (1) type-scale discipline — font sizes not derived from one ratio, or font/weight counts over a cap; (2) line length — paragraph measure outside 45-75 characters; (3) tabular figures — numeric/price/timer UI without tabular-nums. Each finding names the rule violated, per the lens's own Reporting section.

### Key Files

- `plugin/skills/visual-review/ux-heuristics-lens.md` — new checklist rows for type scale, line length, and tabular figures

## Gotchas

- The competitor ("UX engine") mention in Current State is informational only. Shaping dropped the original "note in Impeccable's own docs" deliverable: Impeccable is a third-party plugin this repo does not edit. Evaluating the tool would be a separate record.
